relations.subject: John Caspar Leyden
relations.evidence: His father, a shepherd, had contrived to send him to Edinburgh University to study for the ministry.

relations.subject: John Caspar Leyden
relations.evidence: It was Anderson who later introduced him to Dr Alexander Murray, and Murray, probably, who led him to the study of Eastern languages.

relations.subject: John Caspar Leyden
relations.evidence: Walter Scott, who was then collecting materials for his Minstrelsy of the Scottish Border (1802). Leyden was admirably fitted for helping in this kind of work

relations.subject: John Caspar Leyden
relations.object: College of Fort William in Calcutta
relations.evidence: In 1808, his knowledge of the languages of India procured him an appointment as professor of Hindustani in the College of Fort William in Calcutta.

relations.subject: John Caspar Leyden
relations.evidence: Leyden and Raffles shared a common interest in Eastern languages, and it was during this brief stay that Leyden worked on an English translation of the Malay Annals, which was posthumously published with an introduction by Raffles in 1821.
